description.summary: what the user is doing, for the visual context engine

protocol.description:
The visual context engine builds the user's memory of their own work from what is on screen. The compositor is the only party that knows which window has focus, who owns it, when the user is typing and when the screen must not be looked at. This protocol gives that to the context engine, and to other applications the user lets see it, in a form that carries no content: counts of key presses, never which keys; the existence of a selection, never its text.
The compositor decides who can bind the manager global from the grants of the user. In version 1 only the context engine can bind it, one binding at a time. From version 2 many clients can bind it at the same time. Each client gets a scope, and the compositor sends each client only what its scope allows. The compositor binds a version 1 client only if that client has the engine scope, so a version 1 client sees the protocol as it was.
The compositor names a client by the program of the process that connected, and reads it only when the client connects. A process that turned off PR_SET_DUMPABLE cannot be read and gets no scope. A daemon that turns it off must connect first.
For an unsandboxed client a scope records the user's consent; it is not enforcement. Any program of the same user can read the screen in other ways, or start an allowed program through fork and exec or with LD_PRELOAD. This holds for the engine scope too. For a sandboxed client the scope is enforced, because the sandbox engine names the app.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_context_manager_v1
interface.description: On bind the compositor describes every mapped window, then sends focus and session, and keeps the client current from then on. From version 2 the compositor sends the scope event before all other events.

entry.name: secret
entry.summary: the source marked the content as a secret

entry.name: typing_paused
entry.summary: no printable key for the pause threshold

entry.name: client
entry.summary: a client with the pause scope, such as the bar

request.name: set_paused
request.description:
While paused the compositor sends no window, focus, activity or selection events and fails every capture the engine holds.
A client with the engine scope pauses observation for all clients, and every client gets the paused event with origin engine. A client with the pause scope does the same, with origin client. Any other client pauses only its own stream: only that client gets the paused event, and the streams of other clients continue.

event.name: window
event.description: Its description follows on the new object and ends with done. The identifier is the one its ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 carries.

event.name: input_activity

description.summary: how much the user did in the focused window

event.description: Counts over the last interval, sent only when non-zero. Never the identity of a key. text counts printable keys, edit Backspace and Delete, nav arrows and paging, chords modifier combinations. Text counts are zero while the window is sensitive.

event.name: selection
event.description: Which selection, the window whose client set it, its mime types joined by commas and a size hint in bytes. Never the content.

enum.name: scope
enum.description:
With metadata a client gets the window objects with their app_id, process, sandbox, placement, state, content_type, sensitivity, done and closed events, and the focus, session, input_activity, paused and done events of the manager. It gets no title events and no selection events.
Text adds the title events and the selection events. Text and raw apply only together with metadata: without metadata a client gets no window objects, so text and raw give it nothing.
A client without metadata gets only the scope, paused and revoked events. With pause it can still pause observation for all clients.

entry.name: metadata
entry.summary: windows without titles, focus, session and activity counts

entry.name: text
entry.summary: window titles and selection events; needs metadata

entry.name: raw
entry.summary: captures of the windows the client sees; needs metadata

entry.name: engine
entry.summary: includes metadata, text, raw and pause; flag_sensitive is not rate-limited

entry.name: user
entry.summary: the user removed the grant or refused the client

entry.name: expired
entry.summary: the grant reached its end time or its session ended

event.name: scope
event.description:
Sent on bind before all other events, and again each time the grant of the client changes but stays. When the grant goes, the compositor sends revoked instead. When the scope gets smaller, the compositor sends closed for each window object the client can no longer see, and sends no events that the new scope does not allow.
When the scope gets larger, the compositor sends what the client could not see before, after this event. When the client gains metadata, it gets a window event for each mapped window with all its properties, then focus and session, then the done event of the manager. When the client gains text, it gets a title event for each window it already has, each followed by the done event of that window.

event.name: revoked

description.summary: the grant of this client was withdrawn

event.description:
After this event the manager and all its window objects are inert. The compositor sends no more events on them and ignores all requests except destroy. The client must destroy the objects. To get context again, the client must bind the global again, and the compositor decides again.
A version 1 client does not get this event. The compositor sends closed for each of its window objects and then sends no more events.

request.name: flag_sensitive

description.summary: treat the window as sensitive for a while

request.description:
The engine saw something on screen that should not be captured. The compositor sets engine_flagged for duration_ms and fails captures of the window meanwhile.
The compositor uses at most 600000 ms (10 minutes); a longer duration_ms is cut to that.
Every bound client can send this request. From version 2 the compositor limits the rate for clients without the engine scope: it ignores a request over the limit, and it can make duration_ms shorter. This is not a protocol error. A client must not send more than one request for a window each second.

event.name: process
event.description: The pid the kernel reported for the client; 0 when unknown.

description.summary: the sandbox the client came from
